\par\smallskip\noindent\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}4 published decisions (18 pages), 3 models, 2 repetitions: 24 planned reviews and 120 answer instances. Measured at revision \code{08e15df}. OpenRouter ignores the temperature setting for the Claude and GPT models, so the repetitions sample run-to-run variation. They count as nonpassing with no partial credit. Audited scores apply the same complete two-way source audit as the free cohort (\code{eval/public-refund/results/source-audit.json}). 10/10 scoped integrity checks passed on one eligible bundle, separate from the case denominator. This is retrospective document review of public records that may have appeared in training, not outcome prediction, and the paid cohort is never pooled with the free cohort. \par\smallskip\noindent\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}Every column keeps all planned questions in its denominator. Strict requires a usable answer that the judge marked correct and not abstained, with at least one claim, every claim supported and cited, and every listed citation relevant. This is the free cohort's definition; amendment A2 corrected the cohort report, which had required only one relevant citation per claim. The judge is Qwen 3.8 Max alone: disclosed amendment A1 excluded Grok 4.7 for infrastructure reasons (2 of its first 5 calls timed out at 180 s, and one returned 5,101 completion tokens against a 2,048-token cap), and its partial rows are unused. There is no inter-judge agreement, and the judges are not human-validated. The prompt-only arm is derived from the same answers, so it equals the contract arm by construction and arm differences are not reported. The free cohort used a different judge, so strict rates are not comparable across cohorts. Eligible means the model responded (HTTP 200 with a finish reason); all tried attempts stay in the denominator. 20 trials per arm after 2 warm-ups per arm per model, run sequentially with the models interleaved. Network and provider time were not controlled. Wall is elapsed time and HTTP is transport and remote service time, not isolated model compute. Residual is elapsed time minus HTTP and backoff; it includes harness hashing, ledger and JSON work and is not pure SDK overhead. Intervals are a 10,000-draw percentile bootstrap of the median within model and arm (seeded; computed here in Node, not reused from a saved result); p95 is sample variability, not a confidence limit.
